name: Cat Cow Stretch
intro:
Cat Cow Stretch (Marjaryasana-Bitilasana) is a gentle flowing yoga sequence that helps warm up the spine and improve flexibility. This movement involves alternating between two poses-Cow Pose, where the spine arches and the chest opens, and Cat Pose, where the back rounds and the chin moves towards the chest. Together, these movements create a smooth rhythm that connects breath with motion.

This stretch is commonly practiced at the beginning of yoga sessions to prepare the body for deeper movements. It helps in releasing tension from the back, shoulders, and neck while improving posture and spinal mobility. The coordinated breathing pattern also calms the mind and enhances focus.

Regular practice of Cat Cow Stretch can reduce stiffness caused by prolonged sitting, making it especially beneficial for students and working professionals. It promotes better blood circulation along the spine and helps maintain overall flexibility and balance in the body.

steps.text: Start on all fours with your hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Inhale and drop your belly down, lifting your chest and tailbone (Cow Pose).
Exhale and round your spine upwards, tucking your chin towards your chest (Cat Pose).
Continue flowing between these two positions with your breath.
Move slowly and maintain a steady breathing rhythm.

benefits: Improves flexibility and mobility of the spine
Relieves tension in the back, neck, and shoulders
Stimulates abdominal organs and improves digestion
Increases blood circulation along the spine
Helps reduce stiffness from prolonged sitting
Calms the mind and reduces stress
Improves coordination between breath and movement
Prepares the body for advanced yoga poses
avoid: You have severe back or spinal injuries
You are experiencing intense neck pain
You have wrist pain or weakness (use support if needed)
You feel discomfort while arching or rounding the back
You have recent abdominal or spinal surgery
You have chronic joint issues without proper guidance
